items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond involves three shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: States that three pairs (six electrons) are shared between two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying three shared pairs or six shared electrons.

rubric.why: A correct example shows a substance containing a triple covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as nitrogen (N2) or ethyne.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A triple covalent bond is formed when two atoms share three pairs of electrons (six electrons).
For example, the two nitrogen atoms in N2 share three pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: Explain how a metallic bond holds metal atoms together.

rubric.why: Metal atoms in the metallic structure are positively charged ions or kernels.
rubric.description: Identifies the positively charged metal ions or kernels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the positive metal ions, cations or kernels.

rubric.why: A metallic bond is the attraction between positive metal particles and delocalised electrons.
rubric.description: Describes the attraction between the positive metal particles and the surrounding delocalised electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this attraction and the delocalised electrons.

modelAnswer: A metallic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between positively charged metal ions (kernels) and the sea of delocalised electrons around them.

items.followUp: State how electrons are shared in a polar covalent bond and in a non-polar covalent bond.

rubric.why: Unequal sharing of bonding electrons is the defining distinction for a polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that electrons are shared unequally in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unequal sharing.

rubric.why: Equal sharing of bonding electrons is the defining distinction for a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that electrons are shared equally in a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying equal sharing.

modelAnswer: In a polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are shared unequally between the atoms.
In a non-polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are shared equally between the atoms.
